 Some of Africa’s most beautiful women face a complex hurdle from Trump’s hardline visa policies, as they find it difficult to enter Puerto Rico to showcase their beauty 
 Chinedu Okafor 
 13 November 2026 03:10 PM 
 Miss Universe contestants from Africa may be faced with a unique challenge as they prepare to participate in the latest iteration of the pageant set to be held in Puerto Rico. 
 Contestants take a break during a sponsorship event at Miss Universe 2025.Courtesy of Miss Universe 
 Miss Universe contestants from Africa face challenges participating in the 2026 pageant in Puerto Rico due to strict US travel restrictions.
 Puerto Rico follows US immigration laws, which currently bar nationals from 75 countries, including 26 in Africa, from obtaining immigrant visas.
 Miss Universe Zimbabwe, Roseanna Hall, and Zambia's Pamela Mubanga are among those unable to participate because their US visas were denied.
 Zambia's Miss Universe organizers confirmed Mubanga's withdrawal was due to US travel restrictions, not personal or documentation issues.

 While at first glance, the competition’s destination doesn’t constitute a problem, a deeper look reveals that being a part of the contest may pose a challenge for Africans, given that the Government of Puerto Rico is a territory of the United States of America . 
 The United States, under its current administration , has imposed very strict travel restrictions, especially from countries that are of concern to it. 
 In January 2026, the Trump administration enacted a policy that stopped immigrant visas from being issued to nationals of 75 countries, including 26 in Africa . 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 This policy is also in effect in Puerto Rico, where the 2026 Miss Universe contest is set to be held. 
 As seen in the official portal of the Government of Puerto Rico, “Individuals visiting Puerto Rico have the same immigration restrictions and privileges as if they were visiting any other destination in the U.S. 
 Foreigners visiting PR are also subject to the same U.S. immigration rules and laws, so be sure to comply with immigration and visa requirements.” 
 As reported by the BBC , Miss Universe Zimbabwe Roseanna Hall, along with several other contestants representing African nations, may be unable to participate in this year's pageant in Puerto Rico due to ongoing difficulties in securing United States visas. 
 "We have been back and forth, trying to get my visa approved," Hall said in a video posted on her Instagram page. 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 "Officially, today is the day I was supposed to be leaving for Puerto Rico for the 75th edition of Miss Universe," she added. 
 The Zimbabwean beauty queen is hardly the only contestant from Africa affected, as Zambia’s contender, Pamela Mubanga, withdrew owing to US travel restrictions. 
 This was confirmed in an official statement issued by the Miss Universe organizers in Zambia, which noted that Ms. Mubanga's inability to participate stemmed from prevailing travel restrictions rather than personal circumstances.

 "Unlike situations where a contestant's visa is denied due to personal circumstances, documentation or organisational challenges, Mubanga's situation is linked to the United States' presidential travel restriction affecting Zambia and other African countries," the statement read. 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Mubanga, a 25-year-old nurse, earned the Miss Universe Zambia title on October 8, securing her place as the country's representative at the global pageant. 
 It also mentioned that contestants from five other African countries were dealing with similar visa problems, but did not say which countries were affected. 
 The two African countries were among 19 countries affected by the partial US travel restrictions imposed under Presidential Proclamation 10998, which came into force on January 1, 2026.
